content.comment_body: Hello, I have a new [product_name] with firmware version [version_no]. After setting the correct time and performing a power off/on cycle, the time setting is lost each time. No matter how I set the time, it always resets after a power failure. According to the [document], chapter 4.3.3, "Because [product_name] backs up the internal real-time clock, it continues operation after a power failure. The surrounding temperature affects the backup time. At 25°C, the typical backup time for a [product_name] is 20 days." Am I missing a specific setting? Kind regards, [user_name]
I don't see anything you might be overlooking. The clock should continue running for about 20 days if the [product_name] is without power. I haven't encountered your issue before.
I tested with my [product_name] ([version_no]), and the real-time clock operates normally after power cycling.
Try leaving the device powered on for a few hours, then test again. If the RTC continues to reset, you may want to request a replacement from your seller if it is still under warranty.

analysis.insight_summary: The user reports that the real-time clock (RTC) setting on the [product_name] does not persist after a power cycle, which contradicts the expected backup functionality described in the product documentation. Other users confirm that they do not encounter this issue, pointing toward a possible hardware or configuration problem unique to this case. The main concern is the loss of time settings after power loss, which does not match the documented capabilities.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the product to preserve the real-time clock setting for the stated duration (about 20 days at 25°C) after losing power, as described in the documentation.
